description.narrative: An Agency for Social Protection under the Office of the President of Uzbekistan was set-up in June 2023. The institution is mandated to design, implement, coordinate and monitor the implementation of social protection programmes across various ministries and Government entities. This is a key milestone towards strengthening the institutional architecture of social protection. The Agency will, among other functions manage the National Social Protection Observatory (NSPO). The NSPO supports the M&E Framework of the National Social Protection Strategy. ILO contributed to the development of the Agency through advice on the mandate, functions and organisational set up. It also contributed to setting-up the NSPO. ILO supported constituents to analyse impact of tax reforms on contributory aspects of social protection budget, in particular on pensions.

description.narrative: The Government has extended of coverage with maternity benefits to formally employed women in private sector to which ILO provided technical support ILO provided technical and financial support to the constituents through assessments of national legislation in relation with C183 as well as on transition to formality and facilitation of tripartite discussions on C183 and extending the scope of maternity protection. The diagnostic study on informality from gender perspective with options for extension of maternity benefit to all women in informal economy was produced and validated by the tripartite discussion with the technical and financial support of ILO. The Legal Assessment of National Legislation on C183 was developed by ILO and validated by the tripartite constituents which was developed in relation to the CEACR observations on Uzbekistan. ILO organised capacity building activities to promote transitions to formality covering the issue of maternity protection as well.

description.narrative: The President of Uzbekistan launched in March 2022, the extension of maternity benefits to formally employed women in private sector at the level of Minimum Consumption Expenditure for 4 months. This program started in September 2022 and currently covers more than 7,000 women working in the private sector. It is integrated with the sickness benefits program as the program is being implemented through a Single Registry (the database receives data on each pregnancy case for working women through the sick leave database of the Ministry of Healthcare). The Government is also considering options for further extension of maternity benefits to all women, including in informal employment. ILO has been providing support to constituents on the extension of maternity protection. This included also the comparative review of national legislation compatibility with respect to the Maternity Protection Convention No. 183 which was validated by constituents in August 2022 supporting the Government’s intention to ratify this Convention. The comparative assessment of national legislation with respect to the Social Security Minimum Standards Convention C102 has been validated by constituents in September 2022. Based on results of ILO supported Diagnostics of informal employment from gender perspective from October 2022 to June 2023 policy options for extension of coverage with maternity benefits to informally employed women and unemployment benefits were validated by constituents in May 2023.
